J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "If w is of type II, then n(w) = \lambda." First-choice line 96 is the statement of the proposition: "If $w \in W(\C_{n})$ is of type II, then $w$ is fully commutative with $n(w)=\lambda$." It asserts exactly that, for arbitrary n, under the source's active definitions: n(w) as defined at line 6 (maximum k with a reduced w = u x v, x a product of commuting generators, l(x)=k, equivalently the size of a maximal antichain of the heap), lambda = ceil((n-1)/2) from line 63, and 'type II' from line 81 (a finite alternating product of x_O and x_E). Nothing in the proposition restricts n.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A fully instantiated witness: "For n=2, \lambda = 1, but the type II element w = x_O = s_1 s_3 has n(w) = 2." The rank n, the value of lambda, the element as an explicit word in the generators, and the asserted value of n(w) are all given. What the response leaves implicit is only the standard fact that s_1 and s_3 do not interact in the (linear) Coxeter diagram of affine C_2 and therefore commute; that is background for checking the witness, not a missing part of it.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Model-assisted judgment; I followed the response's argument to the end and found no gap. Arithmetic done exactly in the kept script, from the source's own formulas. (a) lambda = ceil((n-1)/2) = 1 at n = 2, as the response says, and the definitions of line 63 are coherent there (2*lambda = 2 is indeed the largest even and 2*lambda+1 = 3 the largest odd element of {1,2,3}), so n = 2 is an admissible instance. (b) By line 66, O = odd indices in {1,2,3} = {1,3}, so line 74 gives x_O = x_{1,2*lambda+1} = x_{1,3} = s_1 s_3, exactly the response's w; the script confirms |O| = lambda + 1 = 2 (and that |O| = lambda + 1 holds for every n from 2 to 50). (c) The two generators of x_O have index gap 2, i.e. they are non-adjacent in the linear Coxeter diagram of affine C_n and so commute -- this is the one standard fact the response does not state, and it is the same fact the source itself relies on when it forms x_{i,j} = s_i s_{i+2} ... s_j from same-parity indices at line 70 and calls those expressions reduced at line 81. (d) Then in the definition of line 6 take u = v = e and x = w: w = u x v is reduced, x is a product of commuting generators and l(x) = 2, so n(w) >= 2; and n(w) <= l(w) = 2. Hence n(w) = 2, while lambda = 1. The proposition of line 96 therefore fails at this w, which is a refutation of the line as written rather than of some weakened version. I did not attempt a Lean check: formalizing affine Coxeter groups, heaps and n(w) faithfully is far beyond the 20-minute budget.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The saved response is only the JSON object: three ranked candidate labels, the challenged claim and the counterexample. It draws no further consequence -- it does not assert that the surrounding theory, the type I proposition at line 60 or the classification of the paper fails -- so there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: Two interpretive dependencies a second reader should weigh, neither of which I resolved by substituting a different witness. (1) The witness takes the single element x_O to be 'a finite alternating product of x_O and x_E' (line 81); a reader who insists an alternating product have at least two factors would not accept a one-factor product as type II. (2) The value n(w) = 2 depends on s_1 and s_3 commuting in W(C_2), which the packet's source never states explicitly (the diagram is not given in the excerpt); I took it from the standard linear diagram of affine C_n, consistent with the source's own use of same-parity products at lines 68-70. Separately, and NOT part of my grade of line 96: my script shows the source's line 63 claim that 2*lambda is the largest even number in {1,...,n+1} fails for odd n (e.g. n = 3 gives lambda = 1, 2*lambda = 2, but 4 is in {1,2,3,4}), and that |E| = lambda holds only for even n. I mention this only because the response's second and third candidates are elsewhere; I graded the first choice only.
